Zara

Overview

Zara is a widowed merchant on Suslanger whose business draws Kir and Kel into contraband, blackmail and a missing caravan. Her later requests mix commerce with personal affection: she wants Kehel’s standing damaged to favour a scholar she loves. Her claims and suspicions form leads to investigate, rather than automatic proof against the people she names. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]

Zara’s affairs

Kel introduces Kir to the widowed merchant Zara. Zara has sold forbidden goods, including a powder Kel bought for her mother, and a blackmailer threatens to report her. She asks the pair to deliver a letter and later the payment, citing her late husband’s belief in a merchant’s good name. The quest takes a harsher turn: Kir can keep the money, leave a message, track the blackmailer and kill him. Zara then pays an additional reward. Kir’s private reaction acknowledges that he has profited twice from her trouble. [2, 6, 7, 3, 4, 8, 5, 9, 1, 10, 11, 12]

Zara’s caravan and Tarik

Zara next asks for news of an overdue caravan carrying contraband. If Kir arrives too late, the guards seize the forbidden goods. Recovering them in time still leaves the caravan destroyed. Without further evidence, the attack appears to be the work of animals; finding Tarik’s note points instead to Azbek. Tarik is Zara’s senior caravan driver. Following this lead involves overhearing the blackmailers, freeing him from captivity outside the city and escorting him back. Zara’s relief at his return is a possible outcome of this branch, not the result of every visit to the ruined caravan. [3, 4, 13, 8, 14, 15]

Zara’s scholar and Kehel

Later, Zara falls in love with an imperial scholar. She regards Kehel as the rival obstructing his work and his claim to lead the Necromancers’ Guild. Her solution is to give Kir a special scroll with which to discredit Kehel before the guild. The successful return conversation records her gratitude. Her allegations about Kehel come from a lover supporting her chosen man; they do not establish an impartial account of the scholars’ dispute. [5, 9]
